sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1. Rule returnable forthwith.
Ms. Maithili Mehta, the learned APP waives service of notice of rule for and on behalf of the respondent - State of Gujarat.
Ms. Mamta S. Rajput, learned advocate waives service of notice of rule for and on behalf of the for the respondent no.2 - original complainant.

2. By this application under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the applicants-original accused seek to invoke the inherent powers of this Court praying for quashing of the proceedings of the Criminal Case No.5168 of 2022 pending before the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Gandhinagar arising out from the FIR being C.R. No.11191008220476 of 2022 registered with Chandkheda Police Station, Ahmedabad City for the offence punishable under Sections-498A and 114 of IPC read with Sections-3 & 7 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/8912/2025 ORDER DATED: 06/05/2025 undefined of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
3. Heard learned advocates appearing for the respective parties.

sentences.text: 4. Mr. Sankul Kabra, learned advocate appearing for the applicants submits that pursuant to the registration of the FIR, investigation was carried out and ultimately, at the end of day, charge-sheet was submitted before the competent court by the Investigating Officer, which ultimately, culminated into Criminal Case No.5168 of 2022.
As soon as the said fact came to the knowledge of the applicants, they have approached this Hon'ble Court by way of preferring present application.

Learned advocate further submits that during the pendency of present proceedings, the matter has already been settled between the parties and the complainant is not willing to carry out the proceedings further.
The complainant has filed affidavit specifically stating the said fact that if the proceedings of present complaint is quashed, in that event, she has no objection.
An affidavit to that effect has also been filed by the complainant.
It is, therefore, urged that the present application may be allowed.

5. Learned advocate Ms. Mamta S. Rajput, for the respondent no.2 - original complainant has submitted that the respondent no.2 - complainant has remained present before this court through virtual mode and she has no objection, if the proceedings qua the present applicants would be quashed.

Learned advocate further submits that the disputes is settled NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/8912/2025 ORDER DATED: 06/05/2025 undefined between the parties and an affidavit in that regard is already filed by the complainant.

Learned advocate has identified the signature of the complainant as well as identified the respondent no.2 - original complainant, who is present before this Court through virtual mode and also confirmed correctness and genuineness of the affidavit filed by her.
6. Learned APP has submitted that appropriate order may be passed on the strength of the settlement arrived at between the parties.

7. Therefore, since now, the dispute with reference to the impugned FIR is settled and resolved by and between parties, which is confirmed by the original complainant through her learned advocate,
the trial would be futile and any further continuation of proceedings would amount to abuse of process of law.
Therefore, the impugned FIR is required to be quashed and set aside.
The affidavit filed by the respondent no.2- original complainant is ordered to be taken on record.
8. Resultantly, the present application is allowed.

The proceedings of the Criminal Case No.5168 of 2022 pending before the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Gandhinagar arising out from the FIR being C.R. No.11191008220476 of 2022 registered with Chandkheda Police Station,
Ahmedabad City and all other consequential proceedings arising out of said complaint are hereby quashed and set aside qua the applicants herein.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/8912/2025 ORDER DATED: 06/05/2025 undefined
The Registry shall accept the vakalatnama of Ms. Mamta S. Rajput, the learned advocate who appeared on behalf of the respondent no.2-original first informant.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.

(DIVYESH A. JOSHI,J) A. B. VAGHELA Paresh Mafatlal Parmar vs State Of Gujarat on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114450350/
